title: main-sync git-merge-main uses --no-ff so a diverged branch can sync, and its failure path is transactional

sha_binding.verified_source_note: Last commit on this branch touching a non-proof path (round-3 remediation). merge_sha is null pre-merge as the shared evidence contract requires (CEP-E7); it is bound to the real merge commit by post-merge-lane-close.yml.

verified_source_sha_history.superseded_reason: Round-1 head. Superseded by the P1 remediation commit: the --no-ff change made a conflicting merge reachable, and the wrapper failure path popped the lane-state autostash and released the merge mutex while MERGE_HEAD and unmerged index entries were still in the worktree.

Round-2 head. Superseded by the round-3 remediation commit: independent review found that abortInProgressSync collapsed an undeterminable probe result into 'the ref is absent', so a repository that could not answer took the 'nothing to abort' early return and the wrapper popped the autostash and released the mutex anyway -- the same fail-open class as the P1, one layer down; and that the caller-supplied onCommandFailure hook was called unguarded, so a throwing hook escaped runMergeWrapper with the lock held and no structured result.

verdict.statement: git-merge-main built `git merge --ff-only origin/main`, which cannot merge a diverged branch by definition, so main-sync's recommended exit for divergence failed on exactly the condition it exists for -- leaving git-rebase-main, which rewrites history and invalidates every head-pinned governance artifact, as the only operable path. The command is now `git merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main`: it merges a genuinely diverged branch while preserving both sides' commit SHAs byte-for-byte, is deliberately not a bare `git merge` (which would fast-forward a merely-behind branch and make the verb's effect depend on divergence state), and is noninteractive. Permitting a non-fast-forward merge also permits a conflicting one, which exposed a second defect on the same path and was raised as a review P1: the wrapper popped its lane-state autostash and released the merge mutex while MERGE_HEAD and unmerged index entries were still present, stranding lane state in the stash and letting the next lane acquire a mutex over a half-merged worktree. The failure path is now transactional: abortInProgressSync aborts the in-progress merge/rebase and verifies the result before the stash is restored and before the lock is released, and a cleanup that cannot restore the pre-attempt state fails closed with the distinct merge_wrapper_cleanup_failed code, the mutex retained and the stash left intact. All five wrapper safety invariants are preserved; the mutex ordering is hardened, not weakened. Round 3 closed two fail-open residuals found by independent review: an undeterminable probe result (git exit 128) was being read as 'the ref is absent', which sent an unreadable repository down the 'nothing to abort' early return; and the caller-supplied onCommandFailure hook was called unguarded, so a throwing hook escaped runMergeWrapper with the lock held and no structured result. Both now force the fail-closed branch. The fail-closed recovery message also named `pnpm ops:merge-wrapper guard`, which only asserts the lock is held; it now names `pnpm ops:merge-lock release` and prints the git command that actually ran.

mutants.name: ['merge','--no-ff','--no-edit','origin/main'] -> ['merge','--ff-only','origin/main']
mutants.note: Killed behaviourally, not only by shape: 47-50 fail because the merge genuinely does not occur under --ff-only against a real diverged repository.

mutants.name: --no-edit removed
mutants.note: Killed by command-shape assertions ONLY. git merge --no-ff opens $GIT_EDITOR only when run from a terminal and the wrapper spawns git with piped stdio, so --no-edit cannot be made behaviourally load-bearing in this harness. It is the guarantee for tty callers; the shape assertion pins it.

scope_refusals: scripts/ops/merge-wrapper.ts was added to file_scope_lock for the P1 remediation only: the stash pop and the mutex release live there and nowhere else, and correcting the ordering elsewhere would have required re-acquiring a released lock, which is racy. One new optional option, one new result code, one guarded early return.
The dual-root sync-contract persistence defect in scripts/ops/codex-exec.ts was NOT bundled into this blocker fix.
The CPU/RAM scheduling contention observed during E2E runs was NOT bundled into this blocker fix.
No package.json, lockfile, tsconfig or build-config change. No workflow, branch-protection, proof-schema or bypass-flag change.
Four --ff-only occurrences belonging to main-sync's legitimate `git pull --ff-only origin main` were deliberately left unchanged.
known_gaps: A merge that conflicts still requires manual resolution by the operator. The wrapper now leaves the worktree exactly as it found it and reports actionably, but it does not resolve the conflict.

A --no-ff merge advances the branch head by one merge commit, which still moves the PR head SHA and therefore still invalidates head-pinned governance artifacts. This lane makes the sanctioned exit operable and SHA-preserving for existing commits; it does not eliminate re-authorization after a sync.
The cleanup-failure path deliberately leaves the mutex held. Recovery is manual and the message says so; there is no automatic lock expiry short of the lock TTL.
--no-edit is pinned by command-shape assertions only (see mutation M2); it cannot be made behaviourally load-bearing under piped stdio.
